content.title: Stats breakdown from Michigan State-Louisville
content.text: Men’s March Madness: Second round reaction Tonight saw the final games of the men’s NCAA Tournament second round as March Madness continued — but not for the defending champion.The Florida Gators were stunned by an Alvaro Folgueiras 3-pointer from the corner with just 4.5 seconds remaining, as Iowa took a famous 73-72 win.Purdue had already advanced to the Sweet 16 with a 79-69 victory over Miami before Iowa State routed Kentucky 82-63 to join the Boilermakers, reaching its third Sweet 16 in the last five years. St. John’s beat Kansas with a Dylan Darling layup at the buzzer in the most anticipated matchup of the day, while Tennessee held off Virginia.Get March Madness tickets at StubHubShare your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesHere is the team statistical breakdown from Michigan State's 77-69 win over Louisville:FG:Louisville: 26-63Michigan State: 26-553FG:Louisville: 13-37Michigan State: 11-26Rebounds:Louisville: 32Michigan State: 39Assists:Louisville: 16Michigan State: 22Turnovers:Louisville: 11Michigan State: 15Points in the paint:Louisville: 26Michigan State: 24Largest lead:Louisville: 4Michigan State: 13Fears credits teammates after 16-assist performance Getty ImagesJeremy Fears Jr. recorded 16 assists against Louisville, but he deflected credit for his performance to his teammates after the game on the CBS broadcast:💬 "Overall, it’s my teammates. Teammates, they’re making the shots. They’re doing the hard part. I’m just giving them the ball."Izzo on MSU's performance: 'We did a lot of good things'Michigan State coach Tom Izzo spoke on the CBS broadcast about his team's performance:💬 “We actually played so well, we just had some foolish turnovers. Our bigs weren’t very good early. I think everyone was a little nervous. I hate to say that, but we made some boneheaded plays turning the ball over. We did a lot of good things.”Ngongba may play against TCU Brendan Marks/The AthleticNo boot, no knee rover scooter.Looks like injured Duke center Patrick Ngongba may well make his return from lingering foot soreness today vs. No. 9 TCU.Houston vs. Texas A&M preview Getty Images6:10 p.m. ET, TNTHouston enters this matchup with a top-15 offense and a top-five defense, per KenPom, but here’s the reality — Texas A&M can’t afford to sit back. The Aggies have to be aggressive.Yes, the analytics say Houston is elite on defense, but the Cougars haven’t been quite as disruptive as they were a year ago. Teams have found cracks. When opponents shoot 40 percent or better from the field, Houston is just 2-4. That opens the door for an Aggies team that ranks in the top 55 in 3-point percentage and top 50 in offensive efficiency. Playing timid won’t cut it — especially with an Aggies defense that is giving up 78.7 points per game. This game will require Texas A&M to score, plain and simple.The challenge? Finishing inside won’t come easily. Former Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year JoJo Tugler is a force at the rim, so the Aggies will need to lean heavily on their perimeter shooting.Houston counters with one of the most dangerous backcourts in the country — a three-headed monster featuring projected top-seven pick Kingston Flemings (16.4 points per game), Emanuel Sharp (15.3) and Milos Uzan (11.1).Flemings, in particular, is relentless. He lives in the paint and can get to his spots whenever he wants. You’re not stopping him, you’re just hoping to slow him down.Still, Texas A&M has enough firepower to make this interesting. Rashaun Agee leads the way with 14.9 points per game, and the Aggies have the kind of shooting that can flip a game instantly. If Rylan Griffen and X-factor Pop Isaacs get hot, this is a team capable of knocking down 15-plus 3s out of nowhere.So the question becomes: Is today the day everything clicks? SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementScoring leaders from Michigan State-Louisville Getty ImagesScoring leaders from Michigan State's victory over Louisville:Michigan State: Coen Carr (21 points, 8-of-13 FG)Louisville: Ryan Conwell (21 points, 7-of-15 FG)Michigan State seals spot in Sweet 16 Getty ImagesFINAL – Michigan State 77, Louisville 69The Spartans have sealed their spot in the Sweet 16.Jeremy Fears Jr. set a new record for most assists by a Michigan State player in the NCAA Tournament with 16, and Coen Carr put on an offensive showcase with 21 points on 8-13 shooting from the field.Louisville contended with the Spartans for most of the afternoon but never put together a run to take the lead back in the second half.Michigan State will play the winner of UConn and UCLA in Washington, D.C.Izzo improves to 26-9 in second game of tourney weekendsTom Izzo likes to tell players to win the first game of a weekend and he’ll win them the second. He is now 26-9 in the second game of an NCAA Tournament weekend.Seven of those nine losses have come to a No. 1 seed or the eventual national champion.17th Sweet 16 for Tom Izzo Getty ImagesThat’s 17 Sweet 16 advances for Tom Izzo, putting him two wins from his ninth Final Four. But this ends a long drought for Izzo’s Spartans in terms of consecutive appearances in the second weekend. The last time Michigan State got to the regional semifinals two years in a row was when it got there four straight times between 2012-15, the last of those ending in the Final Four. A shocking loss as a No. 2 seed to No. 15 seed Middle Tennessee 10 years ago started a trend of more ups and downs. The Spartans got to the Elite Eight last year, losing to Auburn.Maybe Coen Carr should try to dunk his free throws?SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSigns of life from Louisville2H 0:11 – Michigan State 75, Louisville 69Signs of life from the Cardinals! Ryan Conwell hits a 3-pointer with two Michigan State defenders in close proximity, and Coen Carr misses both of his free-throw attempts.Louisville cuts the deficit to two possessions on a J’Vonne Hadley layup with 11 seconds.Fears keeps adding to Michigan State's leadAdd two more FTs and another assist to that lol.Fears breaks Magic Johnson's MSU record for assists in the NCAA Tournament with his 15th, a breakaway lob to Cooper for an oop. Spartans up 72-59.— Chris Solari (@chrissolari) March 21, 2026 Fears a major contributor in Michigan State's second-half performance Getty ImagesJeremy Fears has played a role in 26 of MSU’s 32 second-half points through scoring or assists, per the broadcast.Louisville's Fru fouls outH2 2:30 – Michigan State 68, Louisville 56Louisville’s Sananda Fru commits his fifth foul trying to defend an alley-oop attempt and leaves the game.Time is running out on the Cardinals to rally back into this one.Davis' future in Chapel Hill in doubtYour browser does not support the video tag.The future of coach Hubert Davis with the Tar Heels is in doubt, with a decision expected some time between Sunday and early next week.North Carolina surrendered a 19-point lead to VCU in the first round on the NCAA Tournament and lost in overtime. The Athletic's Brendan Marks shares the details on the uncertain future of Davis in Chapel Hill.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCardinals' 3-point shooting is keeping Sweet 16 hopes alive Getty ImagesH2 4:06 – Michigan State 66, Louisville 56The Cardinals are still clinging to their Sweet 16 hopes thanks to 6-of-11 3-point shooting this half. But Michigan State is answering their every move and leads by double digits. Coen Carr has reached a double-double with 19 points and 10 rebounds.Michigan State has Sweet 16 in sight Getty ImagesFive-point possession by Michigan State. Jaxon Kohler knocks down a 3 and suddenly the Spartans lead by 13 with 6:12 left. The green and white here in Buffalo have the 17th Sweet 16 under coach Tom Izzo in sight.Michigan State builds 13-point cushionH2 4:23 – Michigan State 66, Louisville 53Michigan State has opened its lead to 13 in this second half.The Spartans earn five points in a single possession, with two free throws off a flagrant foul and a 3-point make from Jaxon Kohler. Louisville's Ryan Conwell hits a long 3-pointer to end the Michigan State run, but Coen Carr answers back with a 3 as the shot clock expires.Zougris foul upgraded to a flagrant 1 Imagn ImagesVangelis Zougris fouled Jaxon Kohler hard under the basket. Definitely a no-easy-basket foul. Kohler hit the floor, and when Zougris reached a hand out to help up the Spartans star, Kohler not only blew it off but walked through Zougris. Jeremy Fears came over to pull his teammate away from the scrum. Jeremy Fears, peacemaker!.The foul was upgraded to a flagrant 1, and Kohler knocked down both free throws.
